articleTitle: South Korea’s Crypto Bill Nears Completion With Exchange and Stablecoin Rules

sources.title: South Korea Folds Crypto Into National Asset Law as Japan Passes Its Own Reform
South Korea Crypto Bill Nears Completion With Exchange and Stablecoin Rules - Bitcoin Foundation

claims.claim: On July 15 2026, South Korea’s Ministry of Economy and Finance announced the National Asset Basic Act, which for the first time in 76 years incorporates digital assets into the legal framework that governs public wealth.
claims.bestSource: South Korea Folds Crypto Into National Asset Law as Japan Passes Its Own Reform
claims.evidence: On July 15, 2026 — the same day Japan's parliament formally voted to reclassify cryptocurrencies as financial products — South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance announced the National Asset Basic Act, declaring it would rewrite the legal foundation of how the government manages public wealth, and for the first time in 76 years, digital assets would be part of that foundation.

claims.claim: The bill, still a proposal, is nearing completion and will establish licensing regimes for crypto exchanges and rules for stablecoin issuance.
claims.bestSource: South Korea Crypto Bill Nears Completion With Exchange and Stablecoin Rules - Bitcoin Foundation
claims.evidence: The framework would set licensing regimes for crypto exchanges and rules for issuing stablecoins, so trading platforms and stablecoin issuers fall under one broader legislative effort. The bill is still a proposal nearing completion, which means the licensing requirements and the stablecoin conditions will be settled as it moves forward. The South Korea crypto bill nears completion with exchange licensing and stablecoin issuance rules, while its separate crypto tax debate intensifies.

claims.claim: The Bank of Korea has demanded that stablecoin issuers hold 51 % bank ownership, arguing that only financially solvent institutions can ensure stability.
claims.bestSource: South Korea Folds Crypto Into National Asset Law as Japan Passes Its Own Reform
claims.evidence: The Bank of Korea demanded 51% bank ownership for stablecoin issuers, insisting that financial institutions with existing solvency and anti-money-laundering requirements were the only entities capable of ensuring stability.
claims.bestPassage: The Bank of Korea demanded 51% bank ownership for stablecoin issuers, insisting that financial institutions with existing solvency and anti-money-laundering requirements were the only entities capable of ensuring stability.

claims.claim: The Financial Services Commission warns that such a requirement could lock technology firms out of stablecoin issuance and suppress competition, citing the EU’s Markets in Crypto‑Assets regulation where most licensed stablecoin issuers are electronic money institutions rather than banks.
claims.bestSource: South Korea Folds Crypto Into National Asset Law as Japan Passes Its Own Reform
claims.evidence: The Financial Services Commission pushed back, warning that such a rule would effectively lock technology firms out of stablecoin issuance and suppress competition — and cited the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, where the majority of licensed stablecoin issuers are electronic money institutions rather than banks, as a counterexample.
